name: reachability
author: 92711a92
description: Checks whether any path exists from a source node to a target node, using breadth-first search. Use it for questions like 'can you get from X to Y at all?', 'is course A (indirectly) a prerequisite of course B?' or 'are these two people connected?'. Works on directed graphs (follows edge direction, so A->B reachable does not imply B->A; set ignore_direction to true to ignore it) and undirected graphs; weights are ignored. Returns reachable (true/false), the fewest-hop path and its hop count when reachable, and how many nodes the source can reach. Source and target must be node ids: use lookup_node first.

graph_id.description: Id of the graph to search.

source.description: Id of the start node, e.g. 'MAA' in airports. Use lookup_node to find ids.

target.description: Id of the node to reach, e.g. 'LIS' in airports.

ignore_direction.description: On a directed graph, treat every edge as two-way. Has no effect on undirected graphs.
